### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. intestinal obstruction in the newborn due to guanylate cyclase 2C deficiency  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.732)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:4688)

**Proposed mechanism:** GUCY2C (HGNC:4688) —DISRUPTS→ Guanylate cyclase signaling pathway (GO:0007211); Guanylate cyclase signaling pathway (GO:0007211) —DECREASES→ cGMP (CHEBI:17034); cGMP (CHEBI:17034) —DECREASES→ Regulation of intestinal smooth muscle contraction (GO:0031316); Regulation of intestinal smooth muscle contraction (GO:0031316) —LEADS_TO→ Intestinal atresia (HP:0002104); Regulation of intestinal smooth muscle contraction (GO:0031316) —LEADS_TO→ Intestinal obstruction in the newborn (HP:0002092). Loss-of-function mutations in GUCY2C disrupt its signaling pathway, leading to decreased cGMP production. Reduced cGMP impacts the regulation of intestinal smooth muscle contraction, ultimately causing phenotypes such as intestinal atresia and intestinal obstruction in newborns.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in GUCY2C with a minor allele frequency greater than 1% in gnomAD, or demonstration that GUCY2C mutations do not affect cGMP signaling or intestinal smooth muscle function in experimental models. _(variant: HGNC:4688)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of GUCY2C in intestinal development and function could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for congenital intestinal anomalies, potentially involving modulation of the cGMP pathway.
